planting.note: Divide and transplant in spring once new growth begins, keeping the plant in a warm, sheltered spot with consistently high humidity while roots re-establish.

directions: Vandenheckei bears elongated, dark green leaves with a thick pale midrib flanked by narrow silvery-white and pale yellow feathering that fades toward the scalloped leaf margin, a softer, more diffuse pattern than the bold rectangular blotches of the Silver Plate Calathea already in this collection. Leaf undersides show a deep wine-purple that intensifies with maturity. Plant in humus-rich, evenly moist soil with high ambient humidity, since its thin leaf blades scorch and curl quickly in dry indoor air. It forms a tidy clumping rosette well suited to terrariums or grouped shade containers.

common_name: Beauty Star Calathea (Soft Pink-Striped Prayer Plant)

planting.note: Divide clumps in spring and keep humidity consistently high while new roots form, since low humidity causes rapid leaf-tip browning in this cultivar.

directions: Beauty Star carries broad, rounded dark green leaves brushed with wide, soft pink pinstripes that fade to cream as each leaf matures, a looser and more painterly pattern than the fine hairline pinstripes of the species type already in this collection, and distinct from the crisp bold white striping of the Goeppertia majestica White Star cultivar. New leaves emerge tightly rolled and deep maroon before unfurling. Grow in bright, indirect light with constant humidity and evenly moist, well-drained soil. Its compact, upright habit makes it a strong houseplant or shaded patio specimen in warm climates.
sources: White Flower Farm — Calathea ornata 'Beauty Star'

common_name: Magic Star Stromanthe (Speckled Variegated Prayer Plant)

planting.note: Divide rooted offsets in spring and keep them warm and consistently humid, misting or using a pebble tray, since thin leaf edges brown quickly in dry air.

directions: Magic Star shows a scattered, speckled variegation of cream and soft pink flecks stippled irregularly across deep green leaf blades, a subtler and more randomized pattern than the bold pink-white-green blocking of Triostar or the fine parallel white pinstripes of Stripestar already in this collection. Leaf undersides are a rich burgundy that shows through as the foliage moves. It demands consistently moist, humus-rich soil and high humidity, since dry air quickly browns its thin leaf edges. Use it as an accent in bright shade, where the flecked variegation catches light differently from every angle.

planting.note: Divide and transplant in spring, keeping newly divided crowns warm and humid until roots establish; this species is sensitive to both dry air and mineral-heavy tap water.

directions: Sometimes still sold under the discouraged trade name Maui Queen, this species produces elongated, pointed dark green leaves marked with narrow silvery-green bands running parallel to the midrib, a slimmer, more feather-like pattern than the broad blotched foliage of most Calathea already in this collection. The leaf underside is a solid deep purple, and the leaves noticeably rise in the evening and lower again by morning. It prefers bright indirect light, evenly moist humus-rich soil, and high humidity, browning at the tips if air is too dry or water too mineral-heavy. Its upright clumping habit makes it a good textural companion to broader-leaved shade tropicals.
sources: Royal Horticultural Society (RHS) Plant Finder — Goeppertia louisae
